SPORT BEATS Medium Tower Game Yard Outdoor Games for Adults and Family Wooden Stacking Games- Includes Rules and Carry Bag-54 Large Blocks I have always wanted a large wood stacking game. I have been over some friend's houses that had an oversized version of the standard game and it was a ton of fun to play in the backyard. This set is not as big as I have seen in the past, but it also makes it a bit more manageable to store.

We played as a family and decided to try out the custom rules. It took us some time to get creative to come up with some rules, but once we did, it was a lot of fun. So, basically, there is a small board where you can write down custom rules, which mean you have to do a certain task depending on the number you pull. For instance, if you pull a block with a '1', maybe you make that person take a drink or if they pull a '2', do some push-ups. You get the point. Anyway, once we made up some rules, we had a blast.

The blocks are very smooth and made with high quality wood. It comes with a bag to hold all the blocks, which, to be honest, is not of the same quality, but it does the trick. The bag is really cheap and I don't expect it to last long. The material will either rip or the zipper will fail. Luckily, I didn't buy this set for the quality of the bag.

This is a great game to play as a family or with some friends.

text_fidelity_a: Hasbro Beyblade Metal Masters Triple Battle Set Action Figure This toy is basically (for those not familiar) a couple of spinning tops that one sets in motion in a thin plastic 'stadium'. The middle of the floor of the stadium is an interchangeable disc with grooves that the tops can fall into in order to get some crazy spinning going. This was tested and played with by a few kids, ages 7 to 12. One was already familiar with this Beyblade series, he told me his got 'stomped on and broken' by another kid, and one can see how that would be easy. The stadium, which keeps the spinning 'tops' from going all over the house, is pretty flimsy. Maybe that's a good thing for careful kids. Out of the box I thought they would be bored pretty quick, but not so! We quickly abandoned the book of rules and started making our own. Best of all, the instructions were so easy, the 10 year old assembled everything. This was pretty major, as he has dexterity issues. This toy was perfect for him. I even sat on the floor and played a few games. Another nice thing about it is that it's good for all ages (over 8 as the box states) as there is an element of luck, thus insuring some wins from younger kids.

I see this dog keeping toddlers entertained, but not elementary school kids. My kids have watched with me YT videos of the $3000 Aibo dog. They were not fooled by this dog. LOL!

Regardless, this is a well made toy. The weakest feature is the voice command. It doesn't work all the time. It comes with 2 rechargeable batteries for the dog, which is great since you can always have one back-up ready to go. The remote takes two triple AAA batteries. This dog is basically room decor for my daughter, she thinks its cute, but she doesn't really play with it. We get the most fun out of it by turning it on and watching our real dogs react to them.
This is a well made toy, but subtracting 1 star for the hit or miss voice commands and the targeted age for this toy.

You definitely would not want to give this toy to a child under the age of three due to a choking hazard. However, for an older child who loves tiny things, they will really enjoy this set.

On the downside, which perhaps is not surprising given the miniscule size of the pieces in this set, and that everything is made of plastic, the carrying case is rather fragile. It is difficult for a coordinated adult, let alone a small child who is not yet very coordinated, to store all the pieces safely inside the carrying case and avoid breaking the catch on the case. There's definitely also going to be a risk that within a short period of time the child you give this toy to will scatter and lose many of the pieces in this toy set.

There is also a potential choking hazard for pets, particularly small cats and dogs, if they try to chew on or eat the tiny parts in this toy set.

You need manually remove the Bingo balls like those plastic car model kits where you have to remove the parts from a plastic frame. Just twist the bingo balls and they will fall off the frame. Some may have rough plastic edges still attached to them, so I use a nail filer to smooth it out. There are 75 bingo balls total. They provide you with 500 bingo chips, 50 game boards, 2 drawstring pouches, and a master board to double check the winning numbers. In terms of storage, I feel the best place to store the bingo balls is actually in the metal cage itself, not the drawstring pouch. BTW, the quality of the bingo balls are pretty good for being plastic. text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Games Apples to Apples 15th Appleversary Edition My boyfriend and I never heard of this game and this is their 15th "Appleversary" Edition.

This game is for ages 12+ with 4-8 players. Included in the box are:
- One game instruction sheet
- 441 Black Apple Cards
- 63 White Apple Cards
- 25 Scoring Tokens

After all the like colored cards are combined and shuffled (good luck shuffling 441 cards; I couldn't do it), the cards get stored face-down in the plastic game tray/box they came in along with the tokens.

The game of play is as follows:
- Each of the 4 or more players are dealt 5 black cards each.
- The one player in each round who is the judge picks one white card and chooses one of the two words on the cards. He or she then says the word out loud and places the card face up on the table.
- The remaining players pick a black card from their hand that they think best describes the word being played. They put that card face own in the center and when all the players have submitted their card, the black cards in the center get mixed up.
- The judge then reads each card aloud and the player who submitted that card makes their case to the judge of why their card best exemplifies the word being played.
- The player who won their case with the judge gets a token.
- The play then continues to the left with the card decks and judging responsibility becoming the role of the next player. Each player whose card count is less than 5 black cards is dealt another card.
- The game ends when there is a winner with four tokens.

What makes this game so much fun is the conversation that occurs when convincing the judge. For instance, the judge might pick the word squishy and a player might pick the card about fish and say something like when you're preparing the fish and stretching it out for cooking it becomes all squishy.

My boyfriend and I loved it and found it hilarious. We even found it more challenging because the two other people we planned to play with weren't available. As a result, we wound up playing two hands a piece with one of us playing one hand when we were the judge. That brought another whole level of ridiculousness to the table. It was difficult not to pick our own selections as winners.

This game is only limited by each player's imagination and ability to argue their case. It's perfect for parties or large gatherings with 4 to 8 players.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Apples to Apples 15th Appleversary Edition

Blue Orange Flash! Lightening Fast Party Family Dice Rolling Game Games, for 2-6 Players, Ages 7+ Flash is a simple yet fun dice game for the entire family. It consists of six sets of six dice, each distinguished by a different color, six numbered chips for scoring, a score pad with eight challenges and a small pencil, and a storage bag and instructions.

Flash is a fast game and this is one of the reasons busy parents and others will enjoy playing it so much. The object of the game is to complete each of the eight challenges faster than your opponents and what makes it move so quickly is that everyone plays at the same time, racing against each other to see who can complete the challenge the most quickly. Unlike Yahtzee and other dice games where each person plays solo while the others wait, this game offers all- out action through each challenge.

What are the challenges in Flash? Well, they are basic numbering combinations such as six of a kind, a straight, etc. It sounds like it might be difficult, but it really isn't because each individual die has a flash (lightning bolt) on one side that counts as a wildcard. All you do is throw your dice, keep the ones that you need, then pick up the other dice and throw them again and again until you meet the challenge. Whoever completes it first yells "Flash" and picks up the highest scoring chip. Everyone else keeps throwing the dice until they get the challenge correct, but they get a lower scoring chip, all the way down to the number 1 chip. Play continues through all of the challenges and the highest scoring player wins.

The simplicity of this game is one of its strongest points and kids seem to like it more than a game such as Yahtzee for several reasons. First, the speed- it's an all- out battle to see who can meet the challenge before anyone else. Second, every challenge is certain to be met, in contrast with Yahtzee where you may or may not be able to complete each of the items on the score sheet. The scoring is simpler, too, and I like that the manufacturer included a small bag in which to place the dice, chips, pencil, and scoring pad because they would eventually get lost without it.

If I had to look for something to criticize with this dice game, it would be the fact that the challenges are really not that challenging. No matter how bad your luck may be, you will be able to complete each and every challenge- usually in two minutes max. It is only a matter of time until you roll the right numbers on the dice and the wildcard flash makes each challenge that much easier to achieve.

Family game night is part of growing up and Flash is a good game to have around on those nights when you want some family entertainment and only have about 20 minutes or less to spare. It's a fun little game that most anyone will find worthwhile and worth playing.
text_fidelity_b: Blue Orange Flash! Lightening Fast Party Family Dice Rolling Game Games, for 2-6 Players, Ages 7+

I don't mind this and neither does my son but if that will be a deal-breaker for you, it's better that you know now. If you squeeze one ear, the horse sings and the mouth moves. If you squeeze the other ear, a random saying will come out. My son loves pressing the ears and then hurries to kneel down and watch the horse's mouth move. He loves hugging this little guy and when he prefers to rock on it, he will bring me the base so I can put it back on- which takes a whole 2 seconds; you just set it down on top of the rocker base, pull the plastic piece over the front bar and close until it clicks. Voila! To make it a rideable toy again, you simply push the button and the plastic piece pops open to release the horse.

I definitely recommend this little horse for 1 year olds and up. At almost 2 years old, my son has a while to go before he won't fit on this anymore. This was definitely a good buy and worth every penny!

Mattel Disney Princess Royal Castle Disney Princess Royal Castle is a cute castle that is sure to be a hit with young princesses everywhere who are addicted to the Disney Princesses and love anything associated with them. This castle is much like other Disney castles available on the market, with a few added accessories and everything a young girl needs to enjoy hours of imaginative play.

I have two girls who have been Disney fanatics since a young age and still love anything related to Disney- especially the princesses. Their love of Belle, Snow White, Sleeping Beauty, Aerial, and the other princesses was reason enough to bring this toy into the house. Taking it from the box and assembling a few items was all it took to get the castle ready for play. In no time at all, they were running upstairs to find all of their Disney Princess dolls and bringing then downstairs to play with their new castle.

Disney Princess Royal Castle is a cute castle and very girly in appearance, making it just right for Disney Princess fans. My girls like the castle and they love anything that accommodates their Disney princess dolls. They also like making up stories as they play, but they and I both agree that this castle isn't they greatest one with which they have played. One reason is the lack of any sound effects, movements, etc. I am thankful that the castle includes no lights or anything that requires batteries, but it would be nice if it at least offered some mechanical movements, sound chips, or something else. Another issue is the small upper level. This is where the bedroom is located and it is much smaller than the area below. It would be better if the two levels were a little more even.

My girls love anything Disney Princess related and they like this castle, but they do not rank it among their favorites and it is easy to see why. The lack of at least a simple sound effect, the small number of accessories, and the lack of folding or another way to make storing easier all add up to an average toy overall.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Disney Princess Royal Castle

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide The 3Doodler Create + is both a toy and an artist's tool. While trying it out the hours flew by, I felt like a little kid playing with new toys on Christmas morning. Despite the fact that it will take a lot of practice before I can make anything useful or artistic, I'm having a blast trying to learn how to make various shapes. The instructions are very basic, but the website has lots of hints, tips, projects, and stencils to download for free. There are quite a few YouTube videos as well.

As the packaging states, the tip gets incredibly hot. However, the pen's design makes holding it and using it comfortable without risk of a burn. There are 2 types of filaments in the kit; ABS and PLA.

PLA is made from sugarcane and cornstarch and is used for plastic cups, cutlery, and other food grade plasticware. It has a lower melting point and a slightly glossier finish but is not as strong as ABS.

ABS requires a higher melting point and has a chemical smell but it is stronger and less likely to break if dropped.

Cleaning it after use is easy. If there is still some of the plastic sticking out from the unheated end of the pen you simply tap one of the speed buttons twice and it goes in reverse. Once the filament clears the gear mechanism, which can be seen through a clear window, it's easy to pull out. If there is no plastic sticking out then simply use the rest of it up or the long tool can be used to push the remainder out once the tip is removed. The kit has tools to accomplish this and more. The website has good visual instruction for removing the plastic.

So far I wrote my dog's name. The second try was legible but more practice is needed. I then made a pyramid. Not too difficult but a bit rough...more practice needed. I have tried to make a long vertical spiral...haven't figured that out yet. I think it's best if I stick with 2 dimensional objects until I am better able to control the pen and it's flow. Once I master that - look out! I'd like to make a small lampshade, Christmas ornaments, and focal beads for jewelry.

Just what I need, another hobby!!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide

NERF Thunderhawk Nerf AccuStrike Mega Toy Blaster - Longest Nerf Blaster - 10 Official AccuStrike Nerf Mega Darts, 10-Dart Clip, Bipod My boys(5, 7, and 10) love Nerf guns. It's been a main request for birthdays and Christmas over the past year. For my 10 year old's last birthday, he requested a Nerf war. It was beyond fun to see the adults(of all ages) getting in on the fun right alongside the children. This one has a cool factor, since it's the longest Nerf gun at the moment and it truly is Mega. You can slide the barrel out to make it longer and slide it back in to make it shorter. It also has a bipod.

On the negative side, it takes up a great deal of room. It's a bit of a pain with its size. It's also so big that it's hard for my boys to use. I tried to use it and it's even awkward for me. I'd recommend this gun more for teens and adults. The only way my boys are really able to use it is with the bipod. It is a bit easier in the shorter length, but it's still heavy and awkward.

It also takes larger bullets than the average Nerf gun. It's a pain to have to worry about buying 2 separate kinds of bullets. All the rest of what we have take the same ones, and it makes things simpler. This gun comes with 10, but my boys lose darts constantly. Many times we discover where they were after the lawnmower turns them to confetti. Prepare for an extra investment if you don't already have other Mega guns.

Overall, if you don't mind buying the bigger bullets that go with this one and you or your child can handle the size, it's a pretty cool gun. My boys have had a hard time overly enjoying it, though, even if they do find it cool.
text_fidelity_b: NERF Thunderhawk Nerf AccuStrike Mega Toy Blaster - Longest Nerf Blaster - 10 Official AccuStrike Nerf Mega Darts, 10-Dart Clip, Bipod

Zobmondo!! GoLo! Golf Dice Game for Families and Kids, Award-Winning Fun Game for Home or Travel, Quick to Learn, For 1+ Players, Ages 6 and Up This game is pretty simple. Each time you take the dice you'll basically be playing nine holes of golf. The dice are set up with 2 for par 3 holes, 2 for par 5, and the remaining 5 for par four holes. When you start you'll roll all 9 dice. You must keep at least one, but can reroll all the others, and you continue to reroll until you've set aside all 9 dice at which point you score the dice.

Its that simple. Lowest score over X number of holes wins (the game suggests playing 8 rounds to simulate a full 4 day golf tournament).

Fun, portable and very easy to play. It does have the downside of basically being completely random, and in someways its a variation on Yahtzee, but its well themed. If you want a good dice game for trips and don't want Yahtzee, this is a good one to choose.

I am a very cautious adult, thus buying this HS340 so that I would have experience under my belt before using a $150 dollar HS175D ( much better than the HS175) drone. LEGO Creator Expert Vestas Wind Turbine 10268 Building Kit (826 Pieces) This LEGO CREATOR EXPERT VESTAS WIND TURBINE BUILDING KIT (10268; 826 Piece) is a fascinating set that’s much more fun than the advertising makes it appear. Its best feature is also its greatest drawback--the huge turbine blades take a lot of space to display and operate. The blades are motorized (with a servo hidden in the “Vestas” box at the top), and when they’re turning, the two house entrance lights turn on. What better way to dramatize the point that a single huge wind turbine can power thousands of homes?

The model is slightly challenging to build, because it calls for a lot of studs-not-on-top assembly. It’s especially interesting to see how the heavy wind turbine assemblage is secured to the base with only LEGO elements. The set does use specialized large green elements around the shaft to hide the battery box and to help hold the wind turbine firmly.

The model also demonstrates the one feature that bothers me about wind turbines as a source of electricity--they are huge, and loom over their surrounding landscape. The little house is dwarfed by the wind turbine. The house is cute, with windows and door that open, a range and sink, a lamp on a table, and a patio with a table and chairs (created from “repurposed” wheel-well elements).

The minifigs (two Vestas engineers, a female homeowner, and a dog) are great. The engineers have a van that holds their work bench and a hand truck loaded with service tanks and a big assortment of tools. The instruction book includes several pages describing the development of wind turbines as a power source, and showing diagrams of how they work to create electricity from wind currents.

The wind turbine on the model can be rotated by hand atop the shaft. Only the wind turbine blades are motorized. The blades are operated by a switch at the bottom of the shaft. The motor and lights run on 6 AA batteries (not included). The trees in the set are made from plants. (My LEGO Wind Turbine set was purchased from a LEGO Shop.)
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert Vestas Wind Turbine 10268 Building Kit (826 Pieces)

LEGO Creator 3in1 Fire Dragon 31102 Building Kit, Cool Buildable Toy for Kids (234 Pieces) & Creator 3in1 Sports Car Toy 31100 Building Kit (134 Pieces) Having built some of the Lego Ninjago dragons lately, I can’t help but compare them to the Creator 3-in-1 Fire Dragon. I know it’s not a really fair comparison since they are two different themes, but my mind did it anyway. The Ninjago dragons look a bit cooler to me, but the Creator dragon doesn’t use any stickers … so it’s a draw in the end.

I think it’s weird the dragon doesn’t have any arms! He has little T-rex hands attached to his wings, but I wish he had arms so he looked cooler when standing up. It can be tricky to balance him on just his hind legs and tail, though it *is* possible.

text_fidelity_a: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad The power wheels kawasaki lil' quad is a great toy for a toddler. You will want to make sure that your little one has enough flat space to drive around because the turning radius is extremely wide. You will need a very large space to make a complete circle. Also, there is no reverse button. You should not ride this near hills, slopes, pools, roads, cars, or anywhere else that could increase the chances of an accident. You should also note that even if the "go" button is not being pressed the quad can reach high speeds if on a steep incline.  It comes with a rechargeable 6v 4Ah battery and charging cord that is to be plugged into a wall outlet (not a ceiling outlet!). Before using for the first time the battery must be charged for 18 hours, and 14 hours after each use. You are warned not to leave the battery charging for longer than 30 hours or it may cause the battery to degrade. The biggest downside is that there is no light to denote the battery is charging or completely charged. You just have to assume it is charging and that the battery is completely charged after you unplug it. It requires about 10 minutes of assembly time (excluding the sticker time). The quad does not come with the stickers already placed, so you will need to place the stickers on yourself. You will need a philips head and a flat head screw driver, all other parts are included. The only problem that I noted was one of the connections would not completely engage. There is a wire that is used to connect the battery one end and then the electrical supply from the "go" but on the handlebar. For some reason I could not get the handlebar connection to completely snap into place. Even though it did not completely connect it was enough for everything to work, so I left it as is. text_fidelity_a:
HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900 I am a solid intermediate (I hesitate to call myself advanced). Put a plane in my hands and I can probably fly it pretty well.

I have had a Night Vapor that I absolutely love to fly when I am too lazy to carry all the gear out to a park. I can fly the Night Vapor around the yard. I wanted something just a little bigger to fly in the small field behind my house. After seeing some videos on YT I could tell this plane can fly nice and slow. I made the mistake of thinking this was a 4 channel airplane when I bought it. I got it home and was a little disappointed when I pulled it out and realized there where no ailerons...until I flew it.

I have to say, this little plane is an excellent little flyer. It literally flies itself. Ultra stable in fast and slow flight. Docile stall tendencies and if you just stop touching the sticks it will roll itself over and be flying straight and level within a second or two. Take off roll is only about 5 or 6 feet if you jump of the power. Landings can be done in about 10-15 feet of concrete if you are good at spot landing. Just remember THIS IS NOT A PLANE FOR WINDY DAYS. As much as it sucks to get a RTF home and not fly it, be patient and wait. Even 5 mph is probably a bit much for this featherweight little plane. Experienced flyers will be able to handle this plane up to 5-8 mph but new guys should wait for calm winds. Since this plane is so light it doesn't really break easy, it just bounces off things. Being inherently dumb I like to do things I probably shouldn't. The result of this is my Champ being bounced off roofs, trees, rocks and pretty much any other object I just can't resist buzzing as close as I can. So far only little scuffs on the foam are the evidence of my wild flying. This little bugger is hard to break!

My Dad is new to RC and as soon as they get another Champ in at the hobby store I am buying him one to learn to fly.

As an experienced flyer I would HIGHLY recommend this for a new flyer or an experienced flyer that wants to have fun in a very big back yard or a small field.

By the way, I still wanted a 4 channel so I went straight back to the hobby store and got a Parkzone T-28 (the ultra micro version that is roughly the same size as the Champ). It is fun and the ailerons allow for more aerobatics but I have to admit the Champ is much more fun in a small field because it is so easy to fly.

I have a lot of airplanes and helis. I can't think of a better plane to learn to fly with. The Night Vapor I mentioned is also super easy to fly but the Champ flies more like the bigger planes so it will make a much better trainer.
text_fidelity_b: HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900

BlueFit German Tiger I Panzer Tank with Remote Control, Battery, Light, Sound, Rotating Turret and Recoil Action When Cannon Artillery Shoots, Mini 1:72 Scale, Assorted Color This this is awesome. For something that easily sits on the palm of your hand the detail is pretty sharp. It honestly looks like a World War ][ Tiger tank with tons of details. I received the standard, mostly green, camouflage there's also a darker camouflage and a blue tank available. Colors appear to ship randomly. Remote control device coloring also seem to match the tank you get.
This little thing really zips around. I was surprised at how quick it gets up and goes. There's also a super speed button on the controller that adds fifty percent to the speed of the tank. There's also engine noises and what I'm guessing are 'track' sounds are this races around. The turret will turn 360° in one direction, I found going one way the barrel would hang up on the antenna but the turret rotation switches back and forth as you rotate. The barrel also raises and lowers as the turret turns. When you press the fire button there's the sound of a cannon firing and the entire tank body recoils backwards.
The remote control takes four double A batteries and the tank itself charges from a cable attached to the side of the remote. Charging time is fairly quick and I've already gotten several hours of fun out of the tank and it's still going strong. The only reason I can't give it four stars is the tank just won't drive in a straight line. You can someone adjust for the tendency to turn by steering left or right as you go but it would have been just that much cooler if it had driven in a straight line. Still, I'm a fully grown adult and this is one of my favorite things. It's just such a gas to play with.
I received this item in exchange for my review.
